end.summary:
• Found the partner that makes 10 in a new situation, including 8+2, 7+3, and 6+4; this skill was shown.
• Practised listing different pairs that make 10: named 5+5, 6+4, and 9+1, but this is not steady yet and needs checking next time.
• At first said 5+5 was the only pair; later corrected this by accepting 9+1 and other pairs as making 10.
• Used fingers to check addition in several examples.
end.parentNote: Asha practised making 10 with fingers and by finding the missing partner. Gauri found partners such as 8 and 2, 7 and 3, and 6 and 4; listing several different pairs still needs more practice. Gauri first mixed up whether 9 and 1 make 10, then corrected it later in the lesson. At home, ask Gauri to find all the pairs that make 10 using ten small objects, then say each pair aloud.
